EZR.P.6.19-22.text: The Returned Exiles Keep the Passover

EZR.P.8.1-14.text: The Exiles Who Returned with Ezra

EZR.1.1-2.text: God moves King Cyrus to send out a proclamation

EZR.1.3-4.text: Cyrus invites God’s people to go and build the temple

EZR.1.5-6.text: Many people prepare to go and rebuild the temple

EZR.1.7-8.text: Cyrus brings out the temple articles for Sheshbazzar

EZR.2.1-2.text: Zerubbabel and others lead the exiles back to Judah

EZR.2.3-6.text: The families of Parosh, Shephatiah, Arah and Pahath-moab

EZR.2.7-10.text: The families of Elam, Zattu, Zaccai and Bani

EZR.2.11-14.text: The families of Bebai, Azgad, Adonikam and Bigvai

EZR.2.15-18.text: The families of Adin, Ater, Bezai and Jorah

EZR.2.19-22.text: Hashum and Gibbar families; men of Bethlehem and Netophah

EZR.2.23-26.text: Men of Anathoth, Kiriath-jearim, Ramah and other towns

EZR.2.27-30.text: People of Michmash, Bethel, Ai, Nebo and Magbish

EZR.2.31-33.text: People of Elam, Harim, Lod, Hadid and Ono

EZR.2.36-39.text: The four families of priests who returned

EZR.2.40-42.text: Levites, singers and gatekeepers who returned

EZR.2.43-46.text: Temple servant families from Ziha to Hanan

EZR.2.47-50.text: More temple servant families, from Giddel to Nephusim

EZR.2.51-54.text: More temple servant families, from Bakbuk to Hatipha

EZR.2.55-58.text: Families of Solomon’s servants; total of 392 servants

EZR.2.59-60.text: Some families cannot prove Israelite descent

EZR.2.61-63.text: Some priests cannot find family records and are excluded

EZR.2.64-65.text: The whole group numbers 42,360, with servants and singers

EZR.2.66-67.text: The returning exiles have 736 horses and other animals

EZR.2.68-69.text: Family heads give gold, silver and garments for the temple

EZR.2.70-70.text: Priests, Levites and other Israelites settle in towns

EZR.3.1-2.text: Jeshua and Zerubbabel begin to build the altar

EZR.3.3-5.text: The Israelites set up the altar and offer sacrifices

EZR.3.6-7.text: The Israelites buy cedar logs for the temple

EZR.3.8-9.text: Levites are appointed to supervise the temple work

EZR.3.10-11.text: Priests and Levites praise God for the new foundation

EZR.3.12-13.text: Older people weep while others shout for joy

EZR.4.1-2.text: Enemies of Judah ask to join in building the temple

EZR.4.3-3.text: Zerubbabel and Jeshua refuse help with the temple

EZR.4.4-5.text: The people of the land discourage the Jews from building

EZR.4.6-6.text: An accusation is made against Judah and Jerusalem

EZR.4.7-8.text: Rehum and Shimshai write against Jerusalem to the king

EZR.4.9-10.text: A letter comes from Rehum, Shimshai and other officials

EZR.4.11-12.text: The letter says the Jews are rebuilding a wicked city

EZR.4.13-13.text: The letter warns that the king will lose tax money

EZR.4.14-16.text: The officials ask the king to search the old records

EZR.4.17-19.text: Artaxerxes replies that a search found the city rebelled

EZR.4.20-22.text: Artaxerxes orders the men to stop rebuilding the city

EZR.4.23-24.text: The officials force the Jews to stop building the temple

EZR.5.1-2.text: Haggai and Zechariah help the Jews begin building again

EZR.5.3-5.text: Tattenai asks the Jews who authorized the building

EZR.5.6-7.text: Tattenai writes a letter to King Darius

EZR.5.8-10.text: Tattenai reports that the Jews are building the temple

EZR.5.11-11.text: The elders say the Jews serve the God of heaven and earth

EZR.5.12-13.text: The Jews explain the exile and Cyrus’s decree

EZR.5.14-15.text: Cyrus returned the temple articles to Sheshbazzar

EZR.5.16-16.text: Sheshbazzar laid the foundation and building continues

EZR.5.17-17.text: Tattenai asks the king to search the records in Babylon

EZR.6.1-2.text: Darius orders a search and a scroll is found

EZR.6.3-5.text: Cyrus ordered the temple rebuilt and its articles returned

EZR.6.6-7.text: Darius tells Tattenai to leave the temple work alone

EZR.6.8-10.text: Darius orders that the Jews be given money and offerings

EZR.6.11-12.text: Darius warns that anyone who changes his decree will be punished

EZR.6.19-20.text: The exiles keep the Passover and the Levites kill the lambs

EZR.6.21-22.text: The Israelites eat the Passover and keep the Feast with joy

EZR.7.1-5.text: Ezra’s family line goes back to Aaron the chief priest

EZR.7.6-7.text: Ezra, a skilled scribe, goes up from Babylon to Jerusalem

EZR.7.8-10.text: Ezra arrives in Jerusalem and gives himself to God’s Law

EZR.7.11-13.text: Artaxerxes lets willing Israelites go to Jerusalem with Ezra

EZR.7.14-16.text: Artaxerxes sends Ezra with silver and gold for God’s house

EZR.7.17-18.text: Artaxerxes tells Ezra to buy offerings with the money

EZR.7.19-20.text: Artaxerxes tells Ezra to deliver the articles to God’s house

EZR.7.21-23.text: Artaxerxes orders the treasurers to give Ezra what he needs

EZR.7.24-24.text: Artaxerxes forbids taxes on the temple workers

EZR.7.25-26.text: Artaxerxes tells Ezra to appoint judges and teach the law

EZR.8.1-3.text: The family heads who return with Ezra are listed

EZR.8.4-7.text: More family heads and their men who return are listed

EZR.8.8-11.text: The list of family heads and their men continues

EZR.8.12-14.text: The list of the families who return with Ezra ends

EZR.8.15-16.text: Ezra finds no Levites and calls for the leaders

EZR.8.17-17.text: Ezra sends leaders to Iddo to ask for ministers

EZR.8.18-20.text: Levites and temple servants come to Ezra

EZR.8.24-25.text: Ezra sets apart twelve priests to carry the offering

EZR.8.26-27.text: Ezra weighs out the silver, gold and articles to the priests

EZR.8.28-30.text: Ezra tells the priests to guard the holy offerings

EZR.8.31-31.text: The group leaves the Ahava Canal and God protects them

EZR.8.32-32.text: Ezra and the people arrive in Jerusalem and rest

EZR.8.33-34.text: The silver, gold and articles are weighed in God’s house

EZR.8.35-36.text: The exiles offer sacrifices and give the king’s edicts

EZR.9.1-2.text: Leaders tell Ezra that Israel has married foreign women

EZR.9.3-4.text: Ezra tears his clothes and sits in horror

EZR.9.5-6.text: Ezra kneels in prayer, ashamed of the people’s guilt

EZR.9.7-7.text: Ezra says the people’s guilt has led to captivity

EZR.9.8-9.text: Ezra says God has shown grace and given new life

EZR.9.10-12.text: Ezra says Israel broke God’s commands about marriage

EZR.9.13-14.text: Ezra fears God’s anger if people marry foreigners again

EZR.9.15-15.text: Ezra says God is righteous and the people are guilty

EZR.10.1-2.text: A large crowd weeps, and Shecaniah speaks of hope

EZR.10.3-4.text: Shecaniah urges Ezra to act and send away foreign wives

EZR.10.5-5.text: Ezra makes the leaders and all Israel take an oath

EZR.10.6-6.text: Ezra mourns and fasts in Jehohanan’s room

EZR.10.7-8.text: A call goes out for all the exiles to gather in Jerusalem

EZR.10.9-10.text: Ezra accuses the men of Judah of unfaithful marriages

EZR.10.11-11.text: Ezra tells the men to confess and leave foreign wives

EZR.10.12-13.text: The assembly agrees but says the work needs more time

EZR.10.14-15.text: The assembly asks leaders to handle the cases town by town

EZR.10.16-17.text: Ezra and the family heads investigate the marriages

EZR.10.18-19.text: Priests pledge to send away foreign wives and bring a ram

EZR.10.20-22.text: Priests from the families of Immer, Harim and Pashhur

EZR.10.23-25.text: Guilty Levites, a singer, gatekeepers and men of Parosh

EZR.10.26-29.text: Guilty men from families of Elam, Zattu, Bebai and Bani

EZR.10.30-32.text: Guilty men from the families of Pahath-moab and Harim

EZR.10.33-36.text: Guilty men from the families of Hashum and Bani

EZR.10.37-40.text: More guilty men from the families of Bani and Binnui

EZR.10.41-44.text: More guilty men from Nebo; all had foreign wives
